title: Credo Brands Marketing Ltd - 544058 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Credo Brands (Mufti) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% YoY to INR125.3 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR26.6 crore (21.2% margin) on higher marketing spend.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 5% YoY to about INR125 crore while gross margin was 61.6-62%. EBITDA declined from about INR31 crore to INR27 crore as advertising, brand building and retail transformation spend rose; PAT was INR2.3 crore (1.8% margin). Management said demand moderated from mid-May and remains measured, and that Mufti 2.0 benefits will take multiple quarters to show in numbers. The company opened 5 stores and closed 7, ending at 427 stores.

financial_highlights.change: down from about INR31 crore YoY

segments.name: Retail stores (EBO)
segments.commentary: Store count 427 after 5 openings and 7 closures in Q1. Average annual revenue per EBO was about INR75 lakh in FY26; management targets mid-single-digit same-store revenue growth in FY27. About 59% of stores are in Tier 2 and 3 cities.

segments.name: Digital / D2C
segments.commentary: A growing share of marketing is going to Google and Meta. Management says it continues to build the D2C business, but no revenue figure was given.

guidance_outlook: Marketing spend to remain at 8%-10% of revenue through FY27; Q1 was about 8.5%.
Same-store revenue growth targeted in the mid-single-digit range for FY27.
Inventory days expected to reduce somewhat, per CFO, though management said inventory days vary by season.
Management declined to give growth numbers for the next 1-2 years, citing uncertain demand and a transformation that may take 2-3 quarters or more to show results.
Store expansion is paused in favour of improving productivity and consolidating the brand; closures of underperforming stores continue.
capex_capacity: Store network: 5 new stores opened and 7 underperforming stores closed in Q1, taking the total to 427.
Ongoing renovation of existing stores under the new retail identity, with lower-productivity locations replaced by experience-led stores.
No plans for a larger inventory base; the merchandise mix is being changed instead.
Management said new stores are generating good revenue, without quantifying it.
demand_pricing: Demand was healthy in April and part of May, then moderated from mid-May; management remains measured on near-term demand.
Discretionary spending is soft and competition is intense; management cited competitors spending 15% or more of revenue on advertising versus Mufti's 8%-10%.
Mufti positions itself in the mid-premium segment and says it will keep pricing there; GP margin is reviewed each season and inflation cycle.
Management said it has had no inventory write-offs in the company's history.

qa_highlights.question: Are there early signs of recovery in discretionary consumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees positive signals from renovated and new stores but said it is too early to project, and it will not give projections.

qa_highlights.question: Does premiumisation work in Tier 2 and 3 cities where about 59% of stores are?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiumisation is store-specific and calibrated to each local market and competitor set; it is not limited to Tier 1 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Is current marketing mainly for existing customers or for new ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: retention of existing customers and acquisition of new footfall.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue growth outpace the roughly INR5 crore YoY increase in marketing spend, and can growth recover within 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not confirm revenue growth above ad spend within a year; it said it is unable to extrapolate growth numbers for the next couple of years, while expecting to return to growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will inventory days hold steady or fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects some reduction; the CEO said inventory is cyclical and the company has had no write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin be cut to fund growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GP and pricing are reviewed every season and it will stay in the mid-premium segment, without committing to a margin cut.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression: EBITDA fell from about INR31 crore to INR27 crore YoY while marketing rose; watch whether revenue growth follows the marketing spend.
Demand softness after mid-May 2026 and geopolitical uncertainty; management gave no quarterly outlook.
Competition from both Indian and foreign apparel brands, with some competitors spending above 15% of revenue on advertising.
Inventory days at 74; management expects a reduction but said levels are cyclical.
Same-store revenue target of mid-single-digit growth against a flat store-count trend and a recent 3-year growth slowdown.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term Mufti 2.0 strategy but cautious on near-term numbers. Management repeatedly declined to give growth targets beyond the current year and said results may take several quarters to show.
key_quotes: For the next 2-odd years, it's going to be very difficult for us to say what exactly the numbers will pan out.
We are spending roughly 8% to 10%, and we intend to continue doing that.
